attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production raster terrain tile source for HARVEST THE NIGHT, a cozy farm that becomes a fortress against zombies at night.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved neutral-day material/style study, a visual reference only. Do not copy its buildings, actors or dense ground detail. Image 2 is the reference sheet, also a style reference only, not an edit target.
Style/medium: hand-crafted low-contrast pixel art with deliberate flat pixel clusters, restrained texture and readable materials. Render as a clearly visible coarse 16 by 16 pixel lattice enlarged to fill the whole square source; no fine subpixel detail.
Composition/framing: ONE fully opaque square material tile filling the image edge to edge, direct top-down surface on a rectangular grid. Final native output is exactly 16x16, contact pivot (8,16); this is a downstream reduction target. No diamond/isometric block or tile shown in perspective. No contact shadow.
Lighting/mood: neutral daytime, very subtle upper-left material highlights; runtime supplies dusk/night lighting.
Constraints: opposite edges join seamlessly when repeated, no frame, border, vignette, central emblem, labels, text, watermark or UI. Calm open areas, no random speckles, dots, flowers, objects, cast shadows, blur, gradients, smooth painting or 3D render. All texture must survive nearest reduction to 16x16.
Primary request: terrain/floor, warm horizontal timber planks for the existing farm dock. Main #8C6239, soft wood shadow #6B4A2C and restrained grain highlight #A87C4E. A fully opaque flat top-down wood surface, not a pile or box. Coarse 16 by 16 cells with TWO thin horizontal plank joins across the full width, identical left and right edge patterns at the same height. Top and bottom rows are the same #8C6239. Boards continue continuously when tiles repeat sideways. One subtle short grain run per board at most. No vertical mortar joints, checkerboard, nails, heavy black outline, bevel framing or border around the square. Low contrast and little variation; clear timber material rather than brick masonry. No diagonal perspective.
attempts.decision: Rejected: nearest reduction lost thin plank joins; overly busy grain and opposite border mismatches.

attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: terrain/floor opaque seamless timber tile, final exactly 16x16 pixels.
Input image: edit target is the generated timber candidate.
Primary request: simplify only this wooden surface to a TRUE coarse 16 by 16 block lattice enlarged across the whole square. Delete all of the many fine grain marks. Fill the tile with flat #8C6239 brown. Keep TWO horizontal plank joins, but make each join EXACTLY ONE of the sixteen coarse lattice rows tall, so nearest reduction cannot miss them. Place these dark #6B4A2C join rows at coarse rows 5 and 11, spanning the entire width. There are 16 coarse rows total. Rows 0 and 15 must both be identical flat #8C6239 across the entire width; the leftmost and rightmost columns have exactly identical colors at every corresponding row. Add just two short connected interior grain runs, each two coarse pixels long in #A87C4E, not touching edges. No other details. Absolutely no fine noise, scattered pixels, nails, frame or perspective. Three calm horizontal boards must still read at 16 pixels, repeated tiles connect continuously, fully opaque, neutral daytime.
attempts.decision: Accepted after native/3x repeated patches, exact borders, raw alpha and day/dusk/night Godot actor/farm review.
